claim: Methods for analysing correlated mutations in proteins are becoming an increasingly powerful tool for predicting contacts within and between proteins.
source: Methods for analysing correlated mutations in proteins are becoming an increasingly powerful tool for predicting contacts within and between proteins.
evidence: This is a general statement about the field supported by the context of the manuscript and established scientific knowledge.

claim: Limitations remain due to the requirement for large multiple sequence alignments (MSA).
source: Nevertheless, limitations remain due to the requirement for large multiple sequence alignments (MSA) and the fact that, in general, only the relatively small number of top-ranking predictions are reliable.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation in the field.

claim: Only the relatively small number of top-ranking predictions are reliable in correlated mutation analysis.
source: Nevertheless, limitations remain due to the requirement for large multiple sequence alignments (MSA) and the fact that, in general, only the relatively small number of top-ranking predictions are reliable.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation in the field.

claim: Methods for analysing correlated mutations have relied exclusively on amino acid MSAs as inputs to date.
source: To date, methods for analysing correlated mutations have relied exclusively on amino acid MSAs as inputs.
evidence: This is a statement about the historical state of the field.

claim: A direct contact is more likely to be present when the correlation between the positions is strong at the amino acid level but weak at the codon level.
source: We show that a direct contact is more likely to be present when the correlation between the positions is strong at the amino acid level but weak at the codon level.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The performance of different methods for analysing correlated mutations in predicting contacts is enhanced significantly when amino acid and codon data are combined.
source: The performance of different methods for analysing correlated mutations in predicting contacts is shown to be enhanced significantly when amino acid and codon data are combined.
evidence: This is a main finding supported by the data presented in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Most compensatory mutations occur at positions that are close in space.
source: It has often been assumed, however, that most compensatory mutations occur at positions that are close in space, thus motivating the development of computational methods for identifying co-evolving positions as distance constraints in protein structure prediction (Göbel et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Methods for correlated mutation analysis will become increasingly more useful in the coming years owing to the explosive growth in sequence data.
source: These methods, which rely on multiple sequence alignments (MSA) of homologous proteins as inputs, will become increasingly more useful in the coming years owing to the explosive growth in sequence data.
evidence: This is a prediction based on trends in data availability.

claim: The various methods for CMA differ in the measures they employ for attaching significance to the correlations.
source: The various methods for CMA that have been developed in the past 15 years differ in the measures they employ for attaching significance to the correlations (Livesay et al., 2012; de Juan et al., 2013; Mao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Statistically significant correlations in MSAs that do not reflect interactions between residues in contact can stem from various indirect physical interactions.
source: Statistically significant correlations in MSAs that do not reflect interactions between residues in contact, that is, false positives, can stem from (i) various indirect physical interactions and (ii) common ancestry.
evidence: This is established knowledge about sources of false positives in CMA.

claim: Statistically significant correlations in MSAs that do not reflect interactions between residues in contact can stem from common ancestry.
source: Statistically significant correlations in MSAs that do not reflect interactions between residues in contact, that is, false positives, can stem from (i) various indirect physical interactions and (ii) common ancestry.
evidence: This is established knowledge about sources of false positives in CMA.

claim: The extent of false positives due to common ancestry is manifested in the large number of correlations between positions in non-interacting proteins when the sequences of non-interacting proteins from the same organism are concatenated and subjected to CMA.
source: The extent of false positives due to the latter source is manifested in the large number of correlations between positions in non-interacting proteins that can be observed when the sequences of non-interacting proteins from the same organism are concatanated and subjected to CMA (Noivirt et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Several methods for removing false positives owing to common ancestry were developed but their success in contact prediction using CMA remained limited.
source: Several methods for removing false positives owing to common ancestry were developed (Pollock et al., 1999; Wollenberg and Atchley, 2000; Noivirt et al., 2005; Dunn et al., 2008) but their success in contact prediction using CMA remained limited.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Methods that remove transitive correlations have been developed in recent years and include Direct Coupling Analysis (DCA), PSICOV, and Gremlin's pseudolikelihood method.
source: Methods that remove such transitive correlations have been developed in recent years and include, for example, Direct Coupling Analysis (DCA or DI for Direct Information) (Weigt et al., 2009; Morcos et al., 2011), Protein Sparse Inverse COVariance (PSICOV) (Jones et al., 2012) and Gremlin's pseudolikelihood method (Kamisetty et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the original papers describing these methods.

claim: DCA, PSICOV, and Gremlin's pseudolikelihood method have been found to be very successful in identifying contacting residues.
source: These methods have been found to be very successful in identifying contacting residues (Marks et al., 2012) and they outperform earlier methods (Mao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: DCA, PSICOV, and Gremlin's pseudolikelihood method outperform earlier methods for correlated mutation analysis.
source: These methods have been found to be very successful in identifying contacting residues (Marks et al., 2012) and they outperform earlier methods (Mao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The accuracy of DCA, PSICOV, and Gremlin's pseudolikelihood method is approximately 80% for the correlations in the top 0.1% ranked by their scores.
source: Nevertheless, their accuracy, which is ∼80% for the correlations in the top 0.1% (ranked by their scores), drops to ∼50% for the top 1% (Mao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The accuracy of DCA, PSICOV, and Gremlin's pseudolikelihood method drops to approximately 50% for the top 1% of correlations.
source: Nevertheless, their accuracy, which is ∼80% for the correlations in the top 0.1% (ranked by their scores), drops to ∼50% for the top 1% (Mao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The number of contacts in a protein with N residues is approximately N.
source: Given that the number of contacts in a protein with N residues is ∼N (Faure et al., 2008), it follows that for proteins with, for example, 100 residues (i.e. with 4560 potential contacts between residues separated by at least 5 residues in the sequence) only about 25% of the contacts (i.e. 23 of the top 1% 46 predictions) will be identified by these CMA methods.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: For proteins with 100 residues, only about 25% of the contacts will be identified by DCA, PSICOV, and Gremlin's pseudolikelihood method.
source: Given that the number of contacts in a protein with N residues is ∼N (Faure et al., 2008), it follows that for proteins with, for example, 100 residues (i.e. with 4560 potential contacts between residues separated by at least 5 residues in the sequence) only about 25% of the contacts (i.e. 23 of the top 1% 46 predictions) will be identified by these CMA methods.
evidence: This is calculated based on the accuracy data cited from previous work.

claim: DCA, PSICOV, and Gremlin's pseudolikelihood method require large MSAs comprising thousands of sequences in order to perform well.
source: In addition, these methods require large MSAs comprising thousands of sequences in order to perform well and such sequence data are not always available.
evidence: This is a known limitation of these methods.

claim: A correlation at the amino acid level between two positions is more likely to reflect a direct interaction if the correlation at the codon level for these positions is weak.
source: The key premise underlying the method introduced here is that a correlation at the amino acid level between two positions is more likely to reflect a direct interaction if the correlation at the codon level for these positions is weak (Figure 1).
evidence: This is the key premise of the new method introduced in this study, illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Cases of strong correlations at both the amino acid and codon levels for a pair of positions are less likely to reflect selection to conserve protein contacts.
source: In other words, it is assumed that cases of strong correlations at both the amino acid and codon levels for a pair of positions are less likely to reflect selection to conserve protein contacts and more likely to reflect selection to conserve interactions involving DNA or RNA and/or common ancestry.
evidence: This is an assumption underlying the new method.

claim: Cases of strong correlations at both the amino acid and codon levels for a pair of positions are more likely to reflect selection to conserve interactions involving DNA or RNA and/or common ancestry.
source: In other words, it is assumed that cases of strong correlations at both the amino acid and codon levels for a pair of positions are less likely to reflect selection to conserve protein contacts and more likely to reflect selection to conserve interactions involving DNA or RNA and/or common ancestry.
evidence: This is an assumption underlying the new method.

claim: The PSICOV and DCA methods outperform the OMES, MI and MIp methods.
source: The results show that the PSICOV and DCA methods outperform the OMES, MI and MIp methods (Figure 2) as established before (Mao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2 and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Combining amino acid and codon data leads to an improvement in the predictions by OMES, MI, DCA and PSICOV.
source: They also show that combining amino acid and codon data leads to an improvement in the predictions by OMES, MI, DCA and PSICOV.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2.

claim: In the case of MIp, no improvement is observed upon combining amino acid and codon data despite the fact that this method performs worse than DCA and PSICOV.
source: In the case of MIp, however, no improvement is observed despite the fact that this method performs worse than DCA and PSICOV.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2.

claim: In MIp, a term called average product correction (APC) is subtracted from the MI score for each pair of positions in order to reduce false positives.
source: In MIp, a term called average product correction (APC) is subtracted from the MI score for each pair of positions in order to reduce false positives.
evidence: This is a description of the MIp method.

claim: Removing the APC correction from PSICOV and including the codon data yielded the best method.
source: Removing this correction from PSICOV where it also exists and including the codon data yielded the best method (Figure 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2.

claim: There is an overlap between the background noise reduced upon including the APC term and codon data.
source: Hence, we can conclude that there is an overlap between the background noise reduced upon including the APC term and codon data and that including the latter can be more advantageous as we observe for PSICOV.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that removing APC and including codon data improves PSICOV performance.

claim: Including codon data can be more advantageous than including the APC term as observed for PSICOV.
source: Hence, we can conclude that there is an overlap between the background noise reduced upon including the APC term and codon data and that including the latter can be more advantageous as we observe for PSICOV.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that removing APC and including codon data improves PSICOV performance.

claim: The extent of improvement in contact prediction increases with increasing values of the power α until a maximum is reached.
source: The extent of improvement increases with increasing values of the power α until a maximum is reached (Figure 3A) at a value of α that depends on the method used and different values of αmax were, therefore, chosen accordingly.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The value of α that maximizes improvement depends on the method used.
source: The extent of improvement increases with increasing values of the power α until a maximum is reached (Figure 3A) at a value of α that depends on the method used and different values of αmax were, therefore, chosen accordingly.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Cross-validation by dividing the MSA data into training and test sets showed that the values of αmax are stable.
source: Cross-validation by dividing the MSA data into training and test sets showed that the values of αmax are stable, that is, they do not vary depending on the set of MSAs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The extent of improvement achieved by incorporating codon data was found to be highly significant as indicated by the p-values obtained using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test and the sign test.
source: The extent of improvement achieved by incorporating codon data was found to be highly significant as indicated by the p-values obtained using both tests (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B with statistical tests.

claim: On average, pairs in direct contact constitute only about 10% of the pairs in contact according to the 'All' definition.
source: It may be seen that, on average, pairs in direct contact constitute only about 10% of the pairs in contact according to the 'All' definition and 30% of the pairs in contact according to the Cβ-based definition (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: On average, pairs in direct contact constitute 30% of the pairs in contact according to the Cβ-based definition.
source: It may be seen that, on average, pairs in direct contact constitute only about 10% of the pairs in contact according to the 'All' definition and 30% of the pairs in contact according to the Cβ-based definition (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The Cβ-based definition of contacts is better than the 'All' definition for identifying direct contacts using DCA when amino acid and codon data are combined.
source: The better success of DCA in identifying contacts according to the Cβ-based definition when amino acid and codon data are combined is, therefore, an important result since more pairs that are in true physical contact are identified in this way.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing that the Cβ-based definition identifies a higher proportion of true physical contacts.

claim: In the cases of PSICOV, OMES and DCA, the maximum improvements in contact prediction upon combining amino acid and codon data are when the distance between Cβ atoms used to define a contact is about 5.5, 7 and 5.5 Å, respectively.
source: It may be seen that, in the cases of PSICOV, OMES and DCA, the maximum improvements in contact prediction upon combining amino acid and codon data are when these distances are about 5.5, 7 and 5.5 Å, respectively, and that, in the cases of DCA and OMES, the improvement decreases dramatically when this distance is >∼10 Å (Figure 4).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4.

claim: In the cases of DCA and OMES, the improvement in contact prediction decreases dramatically when the distance used to define a contact is greater than approximately 10 Å.
source: It may be seen that, in the cases of PSICOV, OMES and DCA, the maximum improvements in contact prediction upon combining amino acid and codon data are when these distances are about 5.5, 7 and 5.5 Å, respectively, and that, in the cases of DCA and OMES, the improvement decreases dramatically when this distance is >∼10 Å (Figure 4).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4.

claim: In the case of MI, the extent of improvement upon combining amino acid and codon data is relatively insensitive to the distance used to define a contact and is maximal when it is approximately 4.5 Å.
source: In the case of MI, the extent of improvement upon combining amino acid and codon data is found to be relatively insensitive to the distance used to define a contact and is maximal when it is ∼4.5 Å (Figure 4).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4.

claim: The improvement in contact prediction upon combining amino acid and codon data is greatest when the distance used for contact definition does not lead to many pairs being defined in contact when in fact they are not in direct physical contact.
source: These data, therefore, show again that the improvement in contact prediction upon combining amino acid and codon data is greatest when the distance used for contact definition does not lead to many pairs being defined in contact when in fact they are not in direct physical contact.
evidence: This is inferred from the data in Figure 4.

claim: The crystal structure of Kex1Δp was solved at a resolution of 2.4 Å.
source: The crystal structure of Kex1Δp was solved at a resolution of 2.4 Å (Shilton et al., 1997) and its MSA consists of 1877 sequences.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the original structure paper.

claim: The MSA of Kex1Δp consists of 1877 sequences.
source: The crystal structure of Kex1Δp was solved at a resolution of 2.4 Å (Shilton et al., 1997) and its MSA consists of 1877 sequences.
evidence: This is data from the analysis performed in this study.

claim: Predictions by DCA with incorporation of codon data are more long-range (in sequence) than those made without incorporation of codon data for Kex1Δp.
source: A comparison of the predictions by the two approaches shows that those made with incorporation of codon data are more long-range (in sequence) and more spread throughout the protein structure than those made without incorporation of codon data.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Predictions by DCA with incorporation of codon data are more spread throughout the protein structure than those made without incorporation of codon data for Kex1Δp.
source: A comparison of the predictions by the two approaches shows that those made with incorporation of codon data are more long-range (in sequence) and more spread throughout the protein structure than those made without incorporation of codon data.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Long-range contacts between different secondary structure elements in Kex1Δp that are predicted only when also the codon data is used include the interactions between Thr148 with Phe185, Ala186 with Leu208 and Leu190 with Leu368.
source: Examples for such long-range contacts between different secondary structure elements in Kex1Δp that are predicted only when also the codon data is used include the interactions between Thr148 with Phe185, Ala186 with Leu208 and Leu190 with Leu368 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Incorporation of codon data can yield predictions of contacts between residues that are distant in sequence and are of more value for structure prediction.
source: This and other examples (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) show that incorporation of codon data can yield predictions of contacts between residues that are distant in sequence and are, thus, of more value for structure prediction.
evidence: This is inferred from the examples shown in Figures 5 and 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Improved contact prediction can be achieved by analysing both amino acid and codon MSAs together.
source: Here, we have shown that improved contact prediction can be achieved by analysing both amino acid and codon MSAs together.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by the data presented.

claim: The premise of the approach is that direct contacts are more likely if the correlation at the amino acid level is high but at the codon level is low.
source: The premise of our approach is that direct contacts are more likely if the correlation at the amino acid level is high but at the codon level is low.
evidence: This is the key premise of the new method.

claim: The score proposed can be used in conjunction with different methods of CMA.
source: The score we propose, which reflects this expectation, can be used in conjunction with different methods of CMA but other possible scores should be examined in future work.
evidence: This is demonstrated by applying the score to multiple CMA methods (OMES, MI, DCA, PSICOV).

claim: Other possible scores should be examined in future work.
source: The score we propose, which reflects this expectation, can be used in conjunction with different methods of CMA but other possible scores should be examined in future work.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future research.

claim: Cases where contacts between residues that are distant in sequence are predicted only by using the combined method exist.
source: Importantly, we find cases where contacts between residues that are distant in sequence and, thus, of greatest value for structure prediction are predicted only by using the combined method.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5.

claim: Future work should test other potential applications of combined analysis of amino acid and codon MSAs such as predicting protein–protein interactions.
source: Future work should test other potential applications of combined analysis of amino acid and codon MSAs such as predicting protein–protein interactions and, more generally, in feature selection in machine learning.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future research.

claim: Future work should test combined analysis of amino acid and codon MSAs in feature selection in machine learning.
source: Future work should test other potential applications of combined analysis of amino acid and codon MSAs such as predicting protein–protein interactions and, more generally, in feature selection in machine learning.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future research.

claim: Protein sequence datasets were collected from Pfam version 27.0 based on representative proteomes at 75% co-membership threshold.
source: Protein sequence datasets were collected from Pfam version 27.0 (Finn et al., 2014) based on representative proteomes (Chen et al., 2011) at 75% co-membership threshold (RP75).
evidence: This describes the data collection methodology.

claim: Protein coding sequences (CDS) of the collected proteins from Pfam were retrieved based on Uniprot cross reference annotations using the EMBL-EBI's WSDbfetch services and Ensembl REST API.
source: Protein coding sequences (CDS) of the collected proteins from Pfam were retrieved based on Uniprot cross reference annotations (for Refseq, Ensembl, EMBL and Ensembelgenomes databases in that order of priority) using the EMBL-EBI's WSDbfetch services (McWilliam et al., 2009) and Ensembl REST API (Beta version) (Yates et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the data collection methodology.

claim: All collected CDSs were aligned in accordance to the Pfam HMM based MSAs using tranalign tool from the EMBOSS package.
source: All collected CDSs were aligned in accordance to the Pfam HMM based MSAs using tranalign tool from the EMBOSS package (Rice et al., 2000).
evidence: This describes the data processing methodology.

claim: Pfam domain families with more than 2000 successfully retrieved coding sequences were used for further analysis (total of 551 MSAs).
source: Pfam domain families with more than 2000 successfully retrieved coding sequences were used for further analysis (total of 551 MSAs).
evidence: This describes the data selection criteria.

claim: Only families with a known crystal structure at a resolution of 3 Å or better and with an overlap of at least 80% of the domain sequence to the ATOM sequence in the solved structure were included in the analysis (total of 460 MSAs).
source: Only families with a known crystal structure at a resolution of 3 Å or better (more than 95% of the families have at least three such structures) and with an overlap of at least 80% of the domain sequence to the ATOM sequence in the solved structure were included in the analysis (total of 460 MSAs).
evidence: This describes the data selection criteria.

claim: The analysis was restricted to proteins with more than 200 residues that have a large number of potential contacts for prediction (114 MSAs).
source: Our analysis was also restricted for proteins with more than 200 residues that have a large number of potential contacts for prediction (114 MSAs).
evidence: This describes the data selection criteria.

claim: The evaluation was based on all structures with the highest resolution (at least 3 Å) but, in cases where families have more than 30 known structures with unique sequences, only 30 with the best resolution were used.
source: The evaluation was based on the all structures with the highest resolution (at least 3 Å) but, in cases where families have more than 30 known structures with unique sequences, only 30 with the best resolution were used (in cases of structures with the same resolution we arbitrarily chose one).
evidence: This describes the evaluation methodology.

claim: Two definitions for a contact between two amino acids were employed: a distance of less than 8 Å between Cβ atoms and a distance of less than 8 Å between any two heavy atoms.
source: Two definitions for a contact between two amino acids were employed: a distance of less than 8 Å between Cβ atoms and a distance of less than 8 Å between any two heavy atoms.
evidence: This describes the contact definition used in the analysis.

claim: Only pairs of residues that are separated by at least five amino acids in the protein sequence were considered.
source: Only pairs of residues that are separated by at least five amino acids in the protein sequence were considered.
evidence: This describes the contact definition used in the analysis.

claim: Accuracy was calculated as the proportion of true contacts from the N pairs with the highest score in that set.
source: Accuracy was calculated as the proportion of true contacts from the N pairs with the highest score in that set.
evidence: This describes the accuracy calculation methodology.

claim: The improvement of the method was evaluated using the difference in the area under the curve (AUC) of the accuracy vs number of predicted pairs relative to the results of the original OMES, MI, MIp, PSICOV and DCA methods.
source: We evaluated the improvement of our method using the difference in the area under the curve (AUC) of the accuracy vs number of predicted pairs of our method relative to the results of the original OMES, MI, MIp, PSICOV and DCA methods.
evidence: This describes the evaluation methodology.

claim: A non-redundant set of 2481 PDB entries with a percentage identity cutoff of 20%, resolution better than 1.6 Å and an R-factor cutoff of 0.25 was downloaded from the pre-compiled CullPDB lists.
source: A non-redundant set of 2481 PDB entries with a percentage identity cutoff of 20%, resolution better than 1.6 Å and an R-factor cutoff of 0.25 was downloaded from the pre-compiled CullPDB lists (Wang and Dunbrack, 2003) at http://dunbrack.fccc.edu/Guoli/pisces_download.php on February 25, 2015.
evidence: This describes the data collection methodology.

claim: Two residues were defined to be in a physical contact if they have at least one pair of atoms with a distance ≤3.5 Å.
source: Two residues were defined to be in a physical contact if they have at least one pair of atoms with a distance ≤3.5 Å.
evidence: This describes the physical contact definition used in the analysis.

claim: Maximal improvement of 3.9% was found for DCA when α is 2.5.
source: Maximal respective improvements of 3.9% and 4.2% were found for DCA and MI when α is 2.5, 17.6% for OMES when α is 1.7 and 1.13% for PSICOV when α is 11.2.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Maximal improvement of 4.2% was found for MI when α is 2.5.
source: Maximal respective improvements of 3.9% and 4.2% were found for DCA and MI when α is 2.5, 17.6% for OMES when α is 1.7 and 1.13% for PSICOV when α is 11.2.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Maximal improvement of 17.6% was found for OMES when α is 1.7.
source: Maximal respective improvements of 3.9% and 4.2% were found for DCA and MI when α is 2.5, 17.6% for OMES when α is 1.7 and 1.13% for PSICOV when α is 11.2.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Maximal improvement of 1.13% was found for PSICOV when α is 11.2.
source: Maximal respective improvements of 3.9% and 4.2% were found for DCA and MI when α is 2.5, 17.6% for OMES when α is 1.7 and 1.13% for PSICOV when α is 11.2.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A.

claim: In the case of OMES, MI and DCA, the mean difference between the values of α which maximizes the median of the percent of AUC improvement for the learning and test sets equals zero.
source: In the case of OMES, MI and DCA, the mean difference between the values of α which maximizes the median of the percent of AUC improvement for the learning and test sets equals zero, thus, reflecting the stability of the values of α.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the case of PSICOV, the variance of the difference between the values of α which maximizes the median of the percent of AUC improvement for the learning and test sets is high due to the asymptotic nature of the median percent of AUC improvement as a function of α.

claim: Atoms can interact with each other even if the distance between them is larger than 3.5 Å via, for example, weak electrostatic interactions.
source: It should be noted that atoms can interact with each other even if the distance between them is larger than 3.5 Å via, for example, weak electrostatic interactions but pairs of atoms which are closer than 3.5 Å can always be considered as interacting.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of atomic interactions.

claim: Pairs of atoms which are closer than 3.5 Å can always be considered as interacting.
source: It should be noted that atoms can interact with each other even if the distance between them is larger than 3.5 Å via, for example, weak electrostatic interactions but pairs of atoms which are closer than 3.5 Å can always be considered as interacting.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of atomic interactions.

claim: Residues were considered as being in contact if the distance between their Cβ atoms is ≤8 Å following the definition used in CASP experiments and other studies.
source: Residues were considered as being in contact if the distance between their Cβ atoms is ≤8 Å following the definition used in CASP experiments (Ezkurdia et al., 2009) and other studies (Kamisetty et al., 2013; Skwark et al., 2014) (see also Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The analysis was done for domains of length between 200 and 500 residues and at least 2000 coding sequences in their MSA.
source: The analysis was done for domains of length between 200 and 500 residues and at least 2000 coding sequences in their MSA.
evidence: This describes the data selection criteria.

claim: In the case of the PSICOV method, only 86 MSAs out of the 114 MSAs were used since the others didn't pass this method's threshold for amino acid sequence diversity.
source: In the case of the PSICOV method (Jones et al., 2012), only 86 MSAs out of the 114 MSAs were used since the others didn't pass this method's threshold for amino acid sequence diversity.

claim: Each MSA included at least one sequence with a known crystal structure at a resolution <3 Å in which at least 80% of all the residues are resolved.
source: Each MSA also included at least one sequence with a known crystal structure at a resolution <3 Å in which at least 80% of all the residues are resolved.
evidence: This describes the data selection criteria.

claim: The contact predictions were made for the seven sequences with available crystal structures that have the highest resolution and that in all cases is <3 Å.
source: The contact predictions were made for the seven sequences with available crystal structures that have the highest resolution and that in all cases is <3 Å.

claim: Kex1Δp is a prohormone-processing carboxypeptidase from Saccharomyces cerevisiae that lacks the acidic domain and membrane-spanning portion of Kex1p.
source: The added value in combining amino acid and codon data can be illustrated for contact prediction by DCA in the case of Kex1Δp, a prohormone-processing carboxypeptidase from Saccharomyces cerevisiae that lacks the acidic domain and membrane-spanning portion of Kex1p.
evidence: This is a description of the protein used as an example.

source: Only families with a known crystal structure at a resolution of 3 Å or better (more than 95% of the families have at least three such structures) and with an overlap of at least 80% of the domain sequence to the ATOM sequence in the solved structure were included in the analysis (total of 460 MSAs).

claim: For 81 MSAs, the accuracy of the contact predictions by DCA increases upon incorporating codon data.
source: Significance levels were determined using two non-parametric tests: (i) the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, which takes into account both the number of MSAs for which the accuracy of the contact predictions increases upon incorporating codon data (e.g., 81 in the case of DCA) and the magnitude of the improvement; and (ii) the sign test, which only considers the number of MSAs with improved accuracy.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the statistical analysis.
